subject: physics
title: Work done by a gas and the first law of thermodynamics
key_idea: A gas that expands at constant pressure does work W = pΔV. The first law is energy conservation: heating a gas and doing work on it both increase its internal energy.

sections.heading: Work done by and on a gas

blocks.text: A gas that changes volume against a pressure transfers energy by work. This section covers how to find that work and its direction.

blocks.label: Work done at constant pressure
where: ΔV is the change in volume (m³)

items: When a gas **expands**, it pushes back its surroundings, so the gas does work **on** the surroundings.
When a gas is **compressed**, the surroundings do work **on** the gas.
The work done by the gas and the work done on the gas have the same size and opposite signs.
On a pressure–volume graph, the work done is the area under the line.
W = pΔV at constant pressure.
Expansion: the gas does work. Compression: work is done on the gas.

blocks.text: The first law is the conservation of energy applied to a gas. It links heating, work and the change in internal energy.

items: The internal energy of a gas increases when energy is transferred **to** it by heating.
It also increases when work is done **on** it, for example when it is compressed.
In words: increase in internal energy = energy transferred in by heating + work done on the gas.
Equivalently: energy transferred in by heating = increase in internal energy + work done by the gas.
For a fixed mass of ideal gas, internal energy depends only on temperature.

items.text: A gas at constant pressure 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa expands from 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to 3.5 × 10⁻³ m³. 200 J is transferred to it by heating. Find the increase in internal energy.

blocks.text: Special cases for an ideal gas

items: **Constant temperature**: internal energy is unchanged, so energy in by heating equals work done by the gas.
**Constant volume**: no work is done, so all the energy transferred in raises the internal energy.
**No energy transfer by heating**: the gas is insulated, so the work done on it increases its internal energy.

diagram.alt: Pick a process on a gas and see the work, the heating and the change in internal energy.
diagram.prompt: Choose a process for a fixed mass of ideal gas.

options.label: Expands slowly at constant temperature
results: Gas does work on its surroundings
options.explanation: Internal energy depends only on temperature, so the energy in by heating equals the work done by the gas.

options.label: Heated at constant volume
options.explanation: With no work, all the energy transferred in raises the internal energy.

options.label: Compressed in an insulated cylinder
results: Work is done on the gas
options.explanation: The work done on the gas is its only energy input, so its internal energy rises.

options.label: Heated at constant pressure and expands
options.explanation: The energy in by heating covers both the work done by the gas and the rise in internal energy.

items: Heating and work done on a gas both raise its internal energy.
For an ideal gas at constant temperature, internal energy does not change.

checks.q: A gas expands at a constant pressure of 2.0 × 10⁵ Pa from 1.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³. Calculate the work done by the gas.
A gas receives 500 J by heating and does 200 J of work on its surroundings. Calculate the increase in its internal energy.
A fixed mass of ideal gas is compressed rapidly in an insulated cylinder. State and explain what happens to its temperature.
checks.a: The temperature rises. Work is done on the gas and no energy is transferred by heating, so the internal energy increases.

blocks.label: First law of thermodynamics
where: ΔU is the increase in internal energy (J)
q is the energy transferred to the system by heating (J)
W is the work done on the system (J)

items: Here W is work done **on** the gas. W is positive for compression and negative when the gas expands.
q is positive when energy is transferred into the gas by heating, and negative when energy leaves it.
For expansion at constant pressure, the work done on the gas is −pΔV.

blocks.label: First law of thermodynamics
where: Q is the energy transferred to the system by heating (J)
ΔU is the increase in internal energy (J)
W is the work done by the system (J)

items: Here W is work done **by** the gas. W is positive when the gas expands and negative when it is compressed.
Q is positive when energy is transferred into the gas by heating, and negative when energy leaves it.
For expansion at constant pressure, the work done by the gas is pΔV.
Constant temperature (ideal gas): ΔU = 0, so Q = W.
Constant volume: W = 0, so Q = ΔU.
Insulated gas: Q = 0, so ΔU = −W. A gas that expands without heating cools down.
